conditions: Experiment 1 used four randomized between-participant study conditions; the focal contrast compared a closed-book reconstruction protocol with an open-book relational-diagram protocol
Experiment 2 manipulated the two focal study protocols within participants with task order counterbalanced, while text structure and final-test format were varied between participants
the source states that total initial activity time was matched between the two focal protocols
population: undergraduate students: 80 participants in Experiment 1 and 120 different participants in Experiment 2
task: study brief expository expository academic texts, complete one of the focal active study protocols, and return for delayed content assessments
Experiment 2 crossed enumeration versus sequence text structures with short-answer versus memory-based relational-diagram final assessments
temporal_scope: same-session initial study phase followed by a final assessment one week later
the closed-book protocol contained an initial study period, a free-reconstruction attempt, a restudy period, and a second free-reconstruction attempt before the delay

relations.description: the closed-book reconstruction protocol yields higher one-week short-answer performance than the open-book relational-diagram protocol in both experiments
in Experiment 2 the closed-book reconstruction protocol also yields higher one-week performance when the final assessment itself requires constructing a relational diagram from memory
the focal intervention comparison is evaluated under the source-stated matching of total initial activity time

initial output is approximately equal across the focal conditions in Experiment 1 but favors the diagram condition in Experiment 2, so the delayed advantage is not reducible to uniformly greater initial output in the reconstruction condition

the delayed memory-based diagram probe supplies a second outcome format for the focal comparison

delayed short-answer responses are scored against source-defined correct content
delayed relational diagrams are scored using source-defined idea units
